description: Returns what Cloudflare saw from AI crawlers BEFORE this server did, when the owner has connected a Cloudflare zone: per-crawler totals (requests at the edge, served from cache, reached the server, blocked at the edge, bytes out), per-company rollups, and any conflicts between the edge's observed behaviour and the site's declared AI policy — e.g. the edge blocking a crawler the policy welcomes. The request log only sees what reached the server; this is the missing before-the-server half. Returns connected=false when no zone is connected.
name: agentimus-read-edge-traffic

checked.description: Present when the blocked traffic behind this conflict was verified against the operator's published addresses. Cloudflare counts crawlers by User-Agent string, which anyone can wear — when verified is 0 and nearly everything proved spoofed, the conflict is demoted to an info note: the edge is stopping an impersonation campaign, not the operator.

sampled.description: Blocked requests in the last-day sample.

spoofed.description: Requests from addresses the operator does not use — something else wearing the name.

unknown.description: Requests whose source could not be determined. Never read these as either verdict.

verified.description: Of those, requests from the operator's own published addresses — the operator really being blocked.

blocked.description: warn only: requests the edge turned away in the window.

passed.description: info only: training-crawler requests that got a page (see crawlers[].served) — robots.txt reads and requests the origin refused are not counted.

recent.description: Of `blocked` (warn) or `passed` (info), how many happened in the last day — what keeps the conflict current. A week of blocking with 1 here is history plus one request.

requests.description: warn only: requests that operator made in the window.

level.description: warn = the edge contradicts the declared policy; info = a declared preference is not enforced, or (see `checked`) the blocked traffic proved to be impostors and the warning stood down.

since.description: Unix time this conflict was first seen. It is forgotten when the conflict stops, so a situation that ends and returns is dated from the return. 0 = not yet stamped.

sinceOf.description: What the timestamp above MEANS: "started" = derived from the stored hourly data, the day the conflict actually began; "atleast" = the condition held on every day we still keep, so it began then or earlier and we cannot say which; "noticed" = no usable history, so this is only when the plugin first saw it; "unknown" = no date at all.

sinceText.description: The one sentence the owner's screens show, in the site's date format and timezone, with the wording that matches sinceOf — e.g. "Started August 26, 2026", "Running since at least July 30, 2026", "First seen August 29, 2026". Quote this rather than re-formatting `since`, so a machine and a human make the same claim.

url.description: Cloudflare dashboard deep link where the owner can act.

connected.description: False = no Cloudflare zone is connected; the data fields are then absent.

blocked.description: Requests the edge turned away without contacting this server.

blockedByYou.description: Whether the owner deliberately blocks this crawler at the origin.

probes.description: Of the blocked requests, how many asked for a file no reader fetches (a .env, a .git folder, a wp-config copy): a scanner using this crawler's name. Never counted as the edge turning this crawler away.

served.description: Requests that got a page: a 2xx the edge let through, not counting /robots.txt reads. Passing the edge is not taking content — a request the origin answered 403 or 404 took nothing.

ua.description: Stable crawler token — same vocabulary as the request log.

edgeError.description: Why the last change to the Cloudflare block rule failed, empty when it holds what it should. A name in edgeNames with an error here may have been unblocked and still be blocked at Cloudflare.

hiddenConflicts.description: Conflicts the owner folded to a slim row on their Request Log. Still ACTIVE, and still counted by read-findings — a fold is tidiness, not a resolution. A conflict leaves both lists only when its situation really ends.

lastError.description: The most recent poll failure, empty after a clean poll.

lastPollAt.description: Unix time of the newest numbers; 0 = never polled.

lastPurgeAt.description: Unix time of the last edge cache purge; 0 = never purged.

lastPurgeCleared.description: How many of them the edge confirmed it dropped. Lower than lastPurgeUrls means a PARTIAL purge — the list goes in batches and one failed partway, so the pages after it are still serving stale copies.

lastPurgeError.description: The most recent purge failure (e.g. the token lacks the Cache Purge permission), empty after a clean purge. Separate from lastError so healthy numbers cannot hide it.

lastPurgeUrls.description: How many URLs the last purge was asked to clear; 0 = never purged, or a purge-everything, which has no list.

probes.description: Of `blocked`, the requests for a file no reader fetches — scanners wearing crawler names (see crawlers[].probes). blocked − probes is what the edge turned away from real crawlers.

title: Get edge traffic from Cloudflare
